### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-memory`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-tenancy-guard.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-tenancy-guard.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f0c0fc895a85c965dddcd9f8314f5fd5f3858d71` — the merge of head `cc6801a0e207fb22d960c8493304f28cb56b5568` into base `b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f0c0fc895a85c965dddcd9f8314f5fd5f3858d71 && git checkout f0c0fc895a85c965dddcd9f8314f5fd5f3858d71
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde cc6801a0e207fb22d960c8493304f28cb56b5568 && git checkout -B drift-repro b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde && git merge --no-ff cc6801a0e207fb22d960c8493304f28cb56b5568

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cc6801a0e207fb22d960c8493304f28cb56b5568`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.driver-read-scope-follows-tenant-wall.ts + .changeset/15212-8a-one-predicate.md, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-tenancy-guard.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/types/src/env.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-upgrade-guide.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer0-verdict-end-to-end.test.ts, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md (D8, D9, D11, D14), and the 13 test files of the diff.

Rendered by an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of the adopting seat (`session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`), read-only: the net diff `origin/main...refs/review/pr-24389` (20 files, +763/−245), the PR body and its one comment, card #15212's body and all 17 comments (stage plan 6251466182 and its four amendments, claim 6251491183, os-dev-report 6254147295), #15831's body, ADR-0131 on `origin/main` `5e979073`, and the 41 check-runs on the head. The head was `cc6801a0e…` at review time, as dispatched. Check-runs: the five required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) and every other run `success`; six full-battery jobs `skipped` as on every PR run. No governed-surface path in the file list; 1,008 changed lines; head repo = base repo; the PR is draft.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Can the recorded verdict be forged? — No caller-reachable path. Right.** `OperationContext.tenantLayer0Verdict` (engine.ts:3390-3422) lives on the engine's middleware context, not on the caller's bag. Every construction site builds the literal with named keys and stores the caller's `query`/`options` under `options`, never spread: `find` :14138, `findOne` :14437, `insert` :15263, `update` :16487, `delete` :19482, `count` :20014, `aggregate` :20428. So a REST body or header, an SDK `options`, an AI tool call (all of which enter through those seven doors) cannot place the member. Hooks receive `HookContext` (:14150-14160: object, event, input, session, provenance, user, api, transaction, ql) — no reference to the operation context. `ExecutionContext` carries no such member, and no `withSystemContext`-style helper exists in core or objectql (grep: none). Repo-wide, the only non-test writer is plugin-security's middleware (security-plugin.ts:4227, after the delegator intersection at :4198); the two test plants (engine-data-events.test.ts:828, engine-driver-read-scope.test.ts:75) go through `engine.registerMiddleware`. That is the one path: a middleware registered on the engine (engine.ts:6516, run in registration order at :6562-6566 on the same `ctx`) can overwrite the member — but such a middleware can equally rewrite `ctx.ast.where` and strip the wall itself, so the forge confers no power a plugin did not already hold; it is composition-level trust, the trust #15813 already placed in this member for the bulk-event producer. The reader parses with the `.strict()` `TenantLayer0VerdictSchema` (spec tenant-layer0-verdict.ts:65-86) and a value that does not parse reads as absent → the engine-side fallback with no admin exemption (engine.ts:6971-6986; pinned at engine-driver-read-scope.test.ts:462-466). Two pre-existing, bounded paths worth naming, both unchanged by this diff: a `beforeFind` hook may set `input.options.tenantId`/`tenantIds`, which `buildDriverOptions` keeps (:6908-6914 fill only `undefined`) — it can add a scope or widen the driver's IN set, but Layer 0's `where` (composed onto the AST at security-plugin.ts:4176-4178 before hooks) still bounds the rows; and the fallback's inputs (`context.tenantId`, `accessible_org_ids`, `isSystem`) are session-derived by REST, not body-derived. Neither widens past Layer 0.

**(b) Under a wall, a wider driver scope for a caller who is neither the exempt PLATFORM_ADMIN nor the verified owner? — None found, with one env-only exception that is in the declared direction (see ②).** Traced on `driverReadScope` (engine.ts:6963-6999) against the pre-PR derivation (old :6832-6838, `execCtx.tenantId` always; `tenantIds` only when `tenancyPostureProvider?.() === 'group'`):
- recorded `organization` — Layer 0 names `context.tenantId` (security-plugin.ts:7447-7449), so the id equals the old active-organization equality; a delegator intersection can only narrow (deny), never re-point;
- recorded `organizations` — the set is the caller's membership or the delegator intersection (a subset); the SQL driver reads `tenantIds` as `IN (…) OR NULL` and does not AND the `tenantId` equality under it (sql-driver.ts:15578-15609), so the engine's `tenantId: active ?? ids[0]` is only the key the driver tests for presence — right;
- recorded `deny` — a group member with an empty set keeps the active organization (same as before), and the `where` already carries `RLS_DENY_FILTER`; isolated with no active organization → no scope, as before (no `execCtx.tenantId` meant no scope then too);
- recorded `none` for a non-exempt caller arises only from `tenancyDisabled` (the engine already excludes the object, before and after, :6887) or `objectHasOrgIdField === false` (no column, or a federated phantom anchor): the SQL driver resolves no tenant column and scoped nothing before either (sql-driver.ts:15585-15586); federated objects are excluded by `isFederated` in both versions;
- a **group system context** exits plugin-security before recording, so it takes the fallback: `organizations` over `accessible_org_ids` with the active organization as `tenantId` — identical to before when a provider is injected;
- a **lean embedding with no SecurityPlugin** and no provider: `resolveEnginePosture()` (:7037-7044) falls through to `resolveTenancyPosture()` (types/env.ts:147-163): env unset → `single` → none (the declared widening); `isolated` → equality (unchanged); `group` → the membership union where the old code gave equality (declared direction, missing table row — ②);
- `platformGlobalObjects` — made total by ADR-0131 D7: a declared object is registered with no organization column and `systemFields.tenant: false`, so Layer 0 records `none` and the SQL driver has no column; `isTenancyDisabled` (object.zod.ts:759-761) reads `tenancy.enabled === false` only, so the fallback still hands a system read's `tenantId` for such an object — harmless at the SQL driver (no column), identical to before;
- the **memory driver** boots only under `single` (seam 1, memory-tenancy-guard.ts:38-39) so under a wall it is moot; under `single` seam 3 (:299-330) now never sees a read scope and the driver answers every organization's rows — the D8/D11 consequence, stated in the PR's acceptance notes, and writes still arrive with the target and are still refused (pinned, schedule-acting-organization.dogfood.test.ts:592-620);
- an **object with no organization column** under a wall: the fallback passes `objectHasOrgIdField: undefined` ("assume tenant object"), the SQL driver resolves no column — same rows as before.
No case narrows below Layer 0's `where`, which is always ANDed in; so no two-answers inconsistency remains in the walled postures.

**(c) `single`: the driver no longer narrows — that is what D8/D11 rule. Right, and stated.** D8: "nothing under `single` — and threads the same value to Layer 0 and to every driver"; D11: "only whether the wall is enforced differs". A `single` install holding several organizations was isolated by the driver alone, by accident; the PR body (Consequence paragraph), the changeset ("Who notices") and the entry's `reason` say so. Where an operator reads it: the changeset → `CHANGELOG.md` of objectql/core/spec at release; the entry → the generated upgrade guide (build-upgrade-guide.ts:135-137). Not stated: a hand-written sentence in `content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx` (whose `single` row at :352 says "exactly one organization" and never says the driver enforces nothing) — docs carrier in ③. D9 already refuses an organization-less system write on that topology (`ambiguous-organization`, core system-write-organization.ts:45-51), so the affected topology is one the record already treats as unsupported for writes.

**(d) Writes. Right.** The insert path passes `{ writeTarget: true }` (engine.ts:15936-15944) and `driverWriteTarget` (:7006-7013) returns the active organization in every posture, with the `group` set beside it; `resolveSystemInsertOrganization`'s derived id still wins through `base.tenantId`. The SQL driver's `injectTenantOnInsert` (sql-driver.ts:15652-15664) stamps from it and the autonumber counter scopes by it (:8255-8260). There is **no engine upsert door** (`ENGINE_UPDATE_UPSERT_REMOVED`, engine.ts:848-853); the SQL driver's `upsert()` is reached only by direct driver callers (e.g. lifecycle-service.ts:1474 with no options), so its cross-organization conflict refusal (`upsertTenantGuard` :8912-8925 → `assertMergeLandedInWrittenOrganization` :9387-9425 → `refuseUpsertConflictOutsideWrittenOrganization`) is untouched by construction — the PR body's "insert and upsert pass `writeTarget: true`" is imprecise on the mechanism, the changeset's "still refused" is true. Pinned both ways (engine-driver-read-scope.test.ts:388-392, :468-472). By-id update and delete take the read scope (:17308, :19818; the cascade rebuild at :19860 re-runs `buildDriverOptions` on options that already carry the scope, so it adds nothing), which is the declared widening under `single`.

**(e) Engine-side fallback. Right; the env-unset case is `single`.** `resolveEnginePosture()` prefers the injected provider (the tenancy service's enforced answer), else `resolveTenancyPosture()`: `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE` unset → `resolveMultiOrgEnabled() ? 'isolated' : 'single'` (types/env.ts:163); an unrecognised value throws and the engine degrades to `isolated` (fail toward the wall). So an embedding that mounts no SecurityPlugin, sets no posture, and passed `context.tenantId` to narrow reads is widened to no scope — the declared Clause-② widening, carried by the changeset and the upgrade guide, with no runtime signal (③). It is the same reading the engine's write refusals already use (:7197), so Layer 0 and the engine cannot disagree on posture.

**(f) The semantic entry. Shape and registration right; one wording under-statement (non-blocking).** `export const entry: SemanticMigration` with `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria` matches `SemanticMigration` (types.ts:99-112) and the precedent `18.action-bulk-dispatch-contract-undeclared.ts`; the filename equals `shardNameFor(18, id)` (build-migration-registry.ts:182-183) and the id line matches the generator's `^ {2}id: '…',$` read (:232); it registers by directory into the `semantic:18` region (registry.ts.template:3367) with no index; `check:spec-changes`/`check:upgrade-guide` are green on the head. No tracker number in any shipped string. Wording: `reason` and `replacement` state D8 and D11 correctly and name both arms left standing; `surface` reads "the update and delete predicates", but by-id update and delete lose the `single` scope as well (:17308, :19818 — a by-id operation records no verdict, so the fallback answers `none` under `single`); the changeset table ("update or delete") is right, the entry under-states. The `surface` field's contract is "dotted surface … e.g. `object.titleFormat`"; this one is a sentence rendered inside a code span (build-upgrade-guide.ts:135) — legible, not wrong.

**(g) #15831 closes by pointer. Right.** Its tripwire `tenant-layer0-verdict-end-to-end.test.ts:181` reads `toBe(2)` on `main` already (D7 made the carve-out structural); with this PR the driver leg is the wall's verdict, so the two legs agree by construction, and the issue's own re-check (`platformGlobalObjects` in `packages/drivers`/`packages/objectql/src`) hits only the registry's column-plan reading and prose, no driver code. The PR carries `Part of #15212` and no closing keyword for #15831 — the pointer close is the seat's act after merge, as the plan row says.

### ② Semver level

- **Arm: `yes (widening)` — right; nothing is narrowed.** Every pre-PR driver scope is either kept (walled member, walled system context naming an organization, `group` member with a provider) or widened to what Layer 0 admits (`single` → none; exempt PLATFORM_ADMIN on a posture-permitting object and the verified owner's read → none). No FROM → TO pair narrows, so `yes (narrowing)`, BREAKING and an ADR-0087 disposition are not owed; `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the changeset arm only (`breakingDeclaration`, :673-686: `narrowing` is the signal, `widening` adds none) and `check-changeset-no-major` holds `yes` to `minor` or above — both green.
- **One widening row the table omits (non-blocking):** no injected posture provider (no `tenancy` service), `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=group`, a context carrying `accessible_org_ids` → before: equality on the active organization (old engine.ts:6833-6838 kept `tenantIds` provider-gated, "fail toward isolation"); now: the membership union (`resolveEnginePosture()` reads the env). It is Layer 0's `group` predicate, so it is inside the declared arm; the entry's "the membership set on group" covers it generically. Add the row to the changeset table if another commit is made on this head; otherwise record it on the card.
- **Levels match what the diff publishes.** `@objectstack/core` `minor`: two new root exports (`computeTenantLayer0Verdict`, `TenantLayer0Input`, core security/index.ts:43-46) — a public-surface addition, graded. `@objectstack/objectql` `minor`: the behaviour widening. `@objectstack/spec` `minor`: the new registry entry (and `yes` takes at least `minor`). `@objectstack/plugin-security` `patch`: `tenant-layer.ts` now imports from core and re-exports the two names from the module — the package index exports neither (grep of plugin-security/src/index.ts: none), its Layer 0 ladder is byte-identical, so no public surface of that package moves. `@objectstack/driver-memory`: docblock-only hunks, no changeset owed. A2 holds: core depends on spec and types only; objectql and plugin-security both already depend on core.
- **Line spelling.** PR body `Clause-②: yes`, changeset `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — `clause2-line.mjs` reads the two as one spelling ("`yes` / `yes (widening)` — a widening. The second spelling is the first"); no gate compares the body line to the changeset line byte-for-byte. Wrong text: none.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions of report 6254147295:
1. **Posture reading (A, `resolveEnginePosture`)** — answered right: D8 derives from "posture and context", and it is the posture the engine's own D9 write refusals read; the env-unset default is `single` (types/env.ts:163). Flag carried: the no-provider + env `group` row above (②).
2. **Deny projection (A, active organization if present)** — answered right: where the wall ran, the deny sentinel is in the `where`; where it did not, `deny` arises only under `group` with an empty set (equality kept) or `isolated` with no active organization (no scope, as before). No carrier.
3. **`objectHasOrgIdField: undefined` in the fallback (A)** — answered right for every driver in reach: the SQL family resolves its own column; the memory driver cannot boot under a wall. No carrier. (Note: `isTenancyDisabled` does not read `systemFields.tenant === false`, so a D7-declared platform-global object on a system read still gets a `tenantId` the SQL driver ignores — pre-existing, harmless.)
4. **PR line spelling (A)** — answered right (②).
5. **Dogfood schedule suites set the engine's provider to `isolated` around the bind (A)** — acceptable as a test-side device; the fixture now models env `isolated` + engine `isolated` while the stack's `tenancy` service answers `single`, a split model the suites' own comments disclose. The honest fixture (B, boot walled with the organizations plugin) is a dogfood-lane candidate; no card needed now.

Deviations:
- **`@objectstack/rest` full suite not run locally** — `Test Core` (six shards, all `success`) owns it on the head; no carrier.
- **Commit trailers** — the 8 branch commits carry neither `Claude-Session:` nor `Co-authored-by:` (counted: 0/8). The landing is a squash; the squash commit message must carry the model-free pair. Carrier: the owning seat at landing (the pre-push hook refuses a model identifier; landed history is not rewritten).
- Worktree detach, `with-fleet.sh --read` refused (GET-only `gh` reads), background test loops — reporting only.

Out-of-scope findings:
1. **`packages/verify/src/harness.ts` `inviteForAudienceGate` comment is stale** (says audience-gate invitations are invisible to fixtures; on `single` an owner now reads them). A one-line docblock correction in a published package; carrier: the next C8 stage that edits `packages/verify` (8b-0b's follow-up or 8c-T), named by plan amendment — a stale comment, not a defect card (filing gate ① is not met).
2. **`[tenant-audit]` WARN for an exempt PLATFORM_ADMIN's cross-tenant predicate update/delete under a wall** — `auditMissingTenant` (sql-driver.ts:15677-15707) fires once per object:op when `tenantId` is absent and `isMultiTenantMode()`; its prescription "Pass tenantId via ExecutionContext" is now wrong for that case (the context carries one; the wall lifted it). Carrier: stage 8c-1 (the chokepoint and audit rework), as the report proposes; the engine could also pass `bypassTenantAudit: true` when the recorded verdict is `none` and the context names an organization — 8c-1's design call.
3. **`time_relative` sweep under `single` with several organizations** — a D8/D11 consequence settled by the ADR; the suite now pins the walled model. No carrier.

Further non-blocking items from this review, each with a carrier:
- **Entry wording** (①f): `surface` should name update and delete "by id or by predicate". Carrier: stage 8e, which edits `packages/spec/src/migrations` and already carries the stage-9 entry's D13 wording (claim 6254514683).
- **PR body mechanism wording** (①d): "insert and upsert pass `writeTarget: true`" — there is no engine upsert door; the driver's refusal holds by construction. A body edit by the seat; nothing ships from it.
- **Operator docs**: `content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx` should state that `single` enforces no organization wall at any layer, the driver included, and that organizations in one `single` install are not kept apart. Carrier: a docs-only PR or stage 8c-1 (the docs-drift run listed 26 affected pages on this head).
- **No runtime signal for the `single` widening** (①e): an embedding that relied on the accidental narrowing learns of it only from the CHANGELOG and the upgrade guide. Accepted as D11's consequence; the release notes (release-owned, compiled from this changeset) lead with it.
